items.title: 52240_Frank _Machito_ Grillo oral history interview
items.q: "110th St. and 5th Ave.", by Noro and Ponce, were out at the same time, did it occur to you that the music industry was getting very competitive"

ctx.x: to the house. His uncle was a tremendous bass player with the Cuarteto Caney, so he had all that thing that you just can't avoid to have because you grew up with it. He had the education of that particular syncopation on the bass, so for him it was very easy to put whatever was lacked that particular part of the bass.

I see, okay. Thus, the mambo officially kicked off. Thus, in 1949 the mambo began after the popularity of "Mambo No. 5", by Perez Prado. There are a lot of good recordings I ahh - "Asia Minor", "El Mambo de Broadway" - Alfredito Valdes - Tito Puente's "Abaniquito", Damiron & Chapousaux's "Anabacoa"; it was a great year for music. When all these records were being heard in El Barrio, ahh "110th St. and 5th Ave.", by Noro and Ponce, were out at the same time, did it occur to you that the music industry was getting…

Well, to us it was good for the music because you just can't have everything. Selfishness or egotism is for people that they don't like what they practice. Is like a good doctor, another doctor comes up with some ideas about an operation or an injection or whatever, and get jealous about the other guy that when he finishes his practice he goes to his house and plays with his children or read the paper, watch baseball or boxing. You have to accept that the other person spends the leisure time in something for…
